name: Presenter To Camera
summary: A person speaks directly to the viewer in a locked or gently drifting medium shot, sometimes with a name tag or a supporting graphic beside them. The scene gives the explainer a human voice and carries claims, reasons and proof in the speaker's own words.
when_to_use: A founder or customer states the problem, the reason or the result in their own words.
To add trust and warmth between product demo scenes.
When a spoken claim needs a quick visual proof card next to the speaker.

slots.name: presenter_clip
slots.what: filmed footage of the speaker, medium or close framing

slots.name: spoken_line
slots.what: the sentence or two the speaker says in this scene

slots.name: name_tag
slots.what: a lower third with the speaker's name and role

slots.name: support_card
slots.what: a window or card that slides in beside the speaker to prove the point

slots.name: keyword
slots.what: one spoken word shown large behind or beside the speaker

steps: Hard cut in on the speaker, usually on a sentence boundary.
The speaker talks with the frame locked or slowly drifting.
A name tag eases in at the lower left early in the first appearance.
Optionally a support card slides in and its content scrolls or appends to prove the claim.
Cut away to a tighter angle or the next scene at the end of the sentence.

build.gsap: One timeline per scene over the footage layer: a short opacity and y tween for the lower third with an ease-out (power family), an x tween sliding any support card in from the side with an ease-out, and a linear y tween for content scrolling inside a masked card; keep the footage itself untouched.
build.remotion: An OffthreadVideo of the presenter in one Sequence; the lower third and support card are child Sequences starting on narration words, each entering with a critically damped spring on translate and opacity, and scrolling content driven by a linear interpolate over the Sequence's frames.

sound: Mostly the speaker's voice over a music bed. When an effect is used it is a reverse swoosh or impact landing on a graphic entrance or a punchy spoken word, with an occasional chime; otherwise no typical sound.
caveats: Measured motion comes from very few videos; most presenter shots have no detected motion event.
Members are mixed: some are plain talking heads, others are graphics laid over or replacing the speaker.
Most of the pattern mix is unnamed, so the named patterns cover only overlay moments.
